mcqs.learning_point: Understand historical development of cell theory
mcqs.question: Which of the following correctly matches the scientist with his contribution to the development of cell theory?

options.A: Robert Hooke – first observed cells in animal tissues.
options.B: Matthias Schleiden – stated that all cells arise from pre‑existing cells.
options.C: Theodor Schwann – proposed that all animals are composed of cells.
options.D: Rudolf Virchow – discovered the cell nucleus.

mcqs.answer: Theodor Schwann – proposed that all animals are composed of cells.
mcqs.explanation: Schwann extended Schleiden's plant cell concept to animals, stating that all animals are made of cells. Hooke observed plant cells, Schleiden formulated the plant part of the theory, and Virchow contributed the idea that all cells arise from pre‑existing cells, not the discovery of the nucleus.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly represents the three main tenets of the cell theory?

options.A: All living organisms are made of cells; cells are the basic unit of structure and function; all cells arise from pre‑existing cells.
options.B: All living organisms are made of cells; cells can arise spontaneously from non‑living matter; cells are the smallest unit of life.
options.C: Only plants are composed of cells; cells are the basic unit of structure; cells can arise spontaneously.
options.D: All living organisms are made of cells; cells contain a nucleus; cells can divide without any pre‑existing cell.

mcqs.answer: All living organisms are made of cells; cells are the basic unit of structure and function; all cells arise from pre‑existing cells.
mcqs.explanation: The classical cell theory consists of three statements: (1) all living things are composed of cells, (2) the cell is the fundamental unit of structure and function, and (3) all cells arise from pre‑existing cells (Virchow). Options B, C, and D each contain an inaccurate statement.

mcqs.question: Which of the following pairs correctly matches an organism with its cellular organization?
mcqs.explanation: Paramecium is a single‑celled protozoan, representing a unicellular organism. Amoeba and bacteria are also unicellular, while oak trees are multicellular. Hence only option B is correct.

mcqs.learning_point: Recognise exceptions and refinements at the required level
mcqs.question: A virologist argues that viruses are not considered cells because they lack a membrane‑bound boundary. Which statement best reflects the accepted refinement to the cell theory regarding such entities?

options.A: Viruses are considered cells because they contain DNA.
options.B: Viruses are living cells that can reproduce independently.
options.C: Viruses are acellular entities and thus are an exception to the statement that all living things are composed of cells.
options.D: Viruses completely disprove the cell theory.

mcqs.answer: Viruses are acellular entities and thus are an exception to the statement that all living things are composed of cells.
mcqs.explanation: Viruses lack a cellular structure; they are acellular. Modern biology refines the cell theory by stating that while all cells arise from pre‑existing cells, some biological agents like viruses are not cells and are treated as exceptions. Options A, B, and D are inaccurate.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand historical development of cell theory
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about the historical development of cell theory is NOT true?

options.A: Robert Hooke coined the term ‘cell’ after observing cork tissue.
options.B: Matthias Schleiden proposed that all plants are composed of cells.
options.C: Theodor Schwann suggested that cells arise spontaneously from non‑living matter.
options.D: Rudolf Virchow added that all cells arise from pre‑existing cells.

mcqs.answer: Theodor Schwann suggested that cells arise spontaneously from non‑living matter.
mcqs.explanation: Schwann extended the cell concept to animals; he never advocated spontaneous generation. The idea of spontaneous generation was disproved long before Schwann. Hooke, Schleiden, and Virchow contributed correctly as described, making option C the false statement.

mcqs.question: If a newly discovered organism performs all life processes but lacks a membrane‑bound boundary, which part of the classical cell theory would need to be reconsidered?

options.A: All living organisms are made of cells.
options.B: Cells are the basic unit of structure and function.
options.C: All cells arise from pre‑existing cells.

mcqs.answer: All living organisms are made of cells.
mcqs.explanation: The organism described is acellular; therefore the statement that every living thing is composed of cells would be challenged. The other statements pertain to properties of cells themselves and would remain valid for true cells.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly differentiates unicellular from multicellular organisms?

options.A: Unicellular organisms have specialized tissues, whereas multicellular organisms do not.
options.B: Multicellular organisms can exhibit cellular differentiation, while unicellular organisms cannot.
options.C: Unicellular organisms reproduce only by binary fission, while multicellular organisms reproduce only by meiosis.
options.D: Multicellular organisms always have a nucleus, whereas unicellular organisms are prokaryotic.

mcqs.answer: Multicellular organisms can exhibit cellular differentiation, while unicellular organisms cannot.
mcqs.explanation: A hallmark of multicellularity is the specialization of cells into different types (differentiation). Unicellular organisms consist of a single cell that performs all functions, so they lack differentiation. Options A, C, and D contain inaccurate generalizations.

mcqs.learning_point: Recognise exceptions and refinements at the required level
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is an accepted refinement to the classical cell theory?

options.A: All viruses are considered cells because they contain genetic material.
options.B: Some cells can arise de novo under laboratory conditions, contradicting Virchow's statement.
options.C: Certain organisms, such as viruses, are acellular and thus are exceptions to the statement that all living things are composed of cells.
options.D: The cell theory states that cells can spontaneously generate, which has been disproved.

mcqs.answer: Certain organisms, such as viruses, are acellular and thus are exceptions to the statement that all living things are composed of cells.
mcqs.explanation: Modern biology refines the cell theory by acknowledging that while the theory holds for cellular life, acellular entities like viruses are exceptions. Options A and B are false, and D misstates the cell theory (it never included spontaneous generation).
